done_when: Find the root cause of each (Forge not waiting for its processes to exit, or the test checking too early or on a reused id) and fix it at the cause; both tests pass on every OS in CI three runs in a row; no test is skipped or loosened to pass

findings.body: The assertion does not establish that exec happened: the original `sh -c sleep 1; exec sleep 30` command already contains `sleep 30`. If the child is delayed beyond the fixed sleep, this test can pass with the original broken `_alive`, because both identity snapshots still describe the shell. Conversely, delaying the first identity read past exec fails line 415 even with correct production code. Synchronize the initial snapshot and wait for an unambiguous command transition before asserting liveness, so this regression test reliably detects the bug.
findings.title: Not done: test_a_process_that_execs_after_it_was_recorded_still_counts_as_running

findings.body: A zombie retains its PID and start time, so this comparison now returns True after termination until the parent reaps it. Previously its changed command made the identity comparison fail. This affects real callers: `_stop` at src/forge/codex.py:373-376 exhausts both waiting periods, and `_take` at lines 408-410 treats a zombie lock owner as still running, preventing doctor from recovering its processes. The timeout cleanup at lines 241-245 also waits to reap its own driver until after `_stop_leftover` returns. Read process state and exclude zombies while preserving identity across exec. See the [Linux wait contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/wait.2.html).
findings.title: Treat terminated, unreaped processes as stopped

why: Main's CI is red on and off: tests/test_codex_record.py::test_6_nothing_left_running fails on macOS and Linux (_down(pid) is False right after the stop), and tests/test_codex_reader.py::test_10_the_cold_read_runs_on_the_other_family fails on Linux (forge doctor doesn't report stopping a crashed forge read's processes), so every pull request hits them
